text.tspan: Anna Kiesenhofer
(born 14 February 1991)
Austrian professional cyclist and mathematician (MSc, PhD.) She won the gold medal in the women's individual road race (137 km) at the
Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics, the first Summer Olympics gold medal for Austria since 2004 and their first cycling Olympic gold medal since 1896.
(Speech at the 19th Vienna Congress 2022)
“My whole life before Tokyo was about hard work and not
having success in the public eye. I had success for myself,
Tokyo was not the first race I competed in. I had so
many small goals I was focusing in on, I was sacrificing
everything for it, and I was often laughed at for
sacrificing so much for seemingly small goals. People will
judge you whether your goals are worth focusing on, and if
they don't seem big enough they will laugh about you when
you work hard. When I don't go to a party just because
I have this little race in my hometown.”
“Thank you very much for this prize. I'm feeling very humbled to receive it.
Thank you also for the nice speeches, especially Manuel, it really touched me.
Yeah, I'm kind of starting to be a role model for people working in science and
sports at the same time and it almost feels a bit strange. Uhm... I have been
hard-working during my whole life and it won't surprise anybody for saying
that in science and in sports you have to be hard-working in order to succeed.
Everybody here, I mean... we have so many famous guests here: Nobel Prize
winners, famous politicians, scientists and yeah... some sports men, women.
Everybody will agree that you have to work hard in order to succeed, but what
I want to say that hard work doesn't guarantee success, hard work is necessary
but hard work is not sufficient at least for having success in the public eye. My
whole life before Tokyo was about hard work and not having success in the
public eye. I had success for myself, Tokyo was not the first race I competed in.
I had so many small goals I was focusing on, I was sacrificing everything for
it, and I was often laughed at for sacrificing so much for seemingly small goals.
People will judge you whether your goals are worth focusing on, and if they
don't seem big enough they will laugh about you when you work hard. When
I don't go to a party just because I have this little race in my hometown.
So yeah, Tokyo was another success for me. It was a really big success, but it
was not so different from the other small successes I had had in the past. What
was really different was the way people viewed me, the perception of the public
changed. Suddenly I was somebody who got invited in by events, who is
supposed to say something intelligent, who is supposed to do things the right
way. It's strange actually, I haven't changed, I'm doing things just the same
way as before, just as right or wrong. I'm certainly not complaining, the success
has opened a lot of doors for me, but I want to always remember where I came
from. Just as in science, in sports the attention goes to a few select people; the
attention, and also the funding. With this speech I want to draw attention to
all the small goals to all the people who sacrifice their free time for things that
are worthwhile for them, but who do not get this recognition.
My Olympic gold medal made me famous, but I do not want it to be some
remote fairy tale of a super talented high achiever that normal people cannot
relate to. I am not a super talented high achiever, I'm a normal person and
this Olympic gold medal stands for all the small successes I had in the past
before the wind that made me famous and it should stand for all the other
small successes that other people have for all the sacrifices that go unnoticed.
It really doesn't matter what goal you are preparing for. It sometimes pains
me when people now approach me and they say: “Okay, I'm not like you, I'm
only a hobby cyclist, I'm only preparing for this or that race, I'm only a
student.” There is no only in a person. There is no only in a goal if it is
important to you. It is not about what is written on a medal that
determines success. It doesn't matter if it says Tokyo or Olympic
or what color it is; this is not what determines success, it is the
obstacles that you overcome towards your success that are
important. Thank you.”
